Dear colleagues,

as part of the 195th European Study Group with Industry (ESGI 195), which will be held 20-24 July 2026 at the University of Exeter, there will be challenge on formalising mathematics in ACL2, sponsored by Kestrel Institute. Specifically, the challenge is focused on formalising Schoof’s Algorithm, or the improved Schoof-Elkies-Atkin (SEA) Algorithm, for counting points on elliptic curves over finite fields in an interactive theorem prover (while the focus will be on ACL2, we are very much interested in transfer to other systems such as Lean, Isabelle, Rocq, etc) and prove its correctness.

For more information about ESGI 195, please see https://mathematics.exeter.ac.uk/esgi/.

For interested participants that cannot self-fund, there is some financial support available. If you want to apply for financial support for your attendance, then please e-mail esgi195@exeter.ac.uk using the subject "Kestrel Institute – ESGI 195". In your email, please include your name, affiliation, position, and what financial support you would like to apply for (accommodation, subsistence, travel). Please also include a short brief of your expertise.

Kind regards and best wishes,
The ESGI 195 Organising & Scientific Committee

Prof. Chris Budd OBE, FIMA, C Math, NTF (University of Bath, UK)
Dr. Dawn Geatches (Innovate UK Business Connect, UK)
Dr. Tony Samuel (University of Exeter, UK)
Prof. Stefan Siegert (University of Exeter, UK)
Dr. Magdalena Strauss (University of Exeter, UK)
